newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-LATE BIRDIES LIFT JOHANSSON PAST ROCCA.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LATE BIRDIES LIFT JOHANSSON PAST ROCCA.

text.p: Sweden's Per-Ulrik Johansson made up for a disappointing season by winning the European Open on Sunday, pipping Italy's Costantino Rocca by a shot after securing two birdies in the final two holes.

Johnansson, who went into the event only 96th on the Order of Merit after just one top 10 finish, earned himself the 125,000 pounds jackpot by holing a 10-foot putt on the 17th and two-putting the par five 18th from 35 feet.
It gave the 29-year-old a final-round 70 and an 11-under-par total of 277 at the K Club outside Dublin, enough to edge out Rocca who could only par the last five holes.
England's Roger Chapman and Scot Andrew Coltart shared third place a stroke further back.

Johansson, whose best performance this year was eighth in last month's US PGA championship, said: "I've played really bad all year except for the PGA and I came here not really expecting to make the halfway cut. I'm really proud of myself."

A play-off looked on the cards when Rocca stood on the tee at the 518-yard last one behind, but he found the rough with his drive, had to lay up short of the lake and then left his pitch 18 feet short. His putt to tie never made it to the hole.
